newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends lower, seen easy on fresh inflows.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends lower, seen easy on fresh inflows.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed lower on Friday at 5.50-6.50 percent, off the day's opening levels of 7.50-8.50 percent, dealers said.
Most of the deals were at 6.50-7.50 percent levels, they said. Dealers attributed the easing of rates to inflow of 39.0 billion rupees on account of repo repurchases.
Call rates are expected to ease further on Saturday if the State Bank of India (SBI) enters market, he said.

A strike at SBI's Bombay office led to the premier bank's absence from the call market for the second successive day. Dealers said the absence of SBI was not felt much because of the good liquidity in the banking system.
The securities market was dull on Friday.
The 12.69 percent government stock rose to 101.40 rupees from its previous close of 101.33 rupees, 12.14 percent 2000 rose to 100.73 rupees from 100.70 rupees.
Yield on treasury bills maturing in April 1998 was unchanged at 8.90 percent, dealers said.

Commercial paper maturing in August and September were quoted at 9.70/9.85 percent in the seconday market and certificate of deposit for three months maturity was quoted at 8.00/8.50 percent in the primary market, a dealer said.
